titleEn: Hands Behind Your Back, Take a Big Breath!

pages.text: "Oh!" Taro flung a stone. It had not reached the dry tree across the sandy shore. The quick-handed monkey had already picked up another.
"I want to throw all the way to that tree." Sharp-eared deer Mumu bounded beside him. "I'll throw with you."
Taro's next stone landed in the sand again. "It won't work!" His hands rushed ahead, throwing stone after stone. Sand showered over a line of ants.
The ants scattered, breaking their line. Mumu stepped back and folded their ears. Taro froze with his hand raised.
"When you're angry, your hands move first, don't they?" Mumu clasped both hands behind their back. "Try this. Hands behind you can't throw anything."
Taro put his hands behind his back, too. They still felt restless. "Next, take a big breath." Mumu puffed out their belly. "Hands Behind Your Back, Take a Big Breath!" Both breathed out slowly.
Taro picked up a branch and tapped the sand twice. "My hands can do this instead!" Their restless feeling slowly settled.
He threw again, but still fell short. His face grew hot. Still, he put his hands behind his back and took a big breath. "That's okay. I'll try again."
Mumu drew three lines in the sand. "One, hands behind my back! Two, a big breath out! Three, then talk!" Taro stepped on each line and repeated the steps.
The ants slowly returned and made their line again. Taro hopped over it into Mumu's arms. With hands behind his back, no one got hurt. "Hands Behind Your Back, Take a Big Breath!"
